featured_reviews.name: Pavan Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
First review
The real stars? That filter coffee—strong, frothy, like a warm hug in a tumbler, cutting through the salty richness perfectly. The payasam, sweet and milky with a cardamom whisper, was pure bliss. Routine dosa didn't disappoint.

Subsequent Review:
When mango season hits Mumbai, Banana Leaf at R City Mall knows exactly how to celebrate it. Their limited-time Mango Mania menu brings together classic South Indian flavors with the king of fruits in a way that feels both comforting and exciting.We started with the ever-reliable Aam Ras with Poori — the kind of pairing that never fails to satisfy. The aam ras was thick, naturally sweet, and bursting with the flavor of ripe mangoes. Paired with soft, fluffy pooris that puffed up perfectly, it made for a simple yet delightful beginning. The Mango Lassi that accompanied it was creamy, chilled, and had just the right balance of sweetness and tang — a refreshing glass that cooled things down instantly.But the real star of the meal was the Mango Pullissery with Neer Dosa. This traditional Kerala-style curry, made with ripe mangoes simmered in a spiced coconut-yogurt gravy (with subtle notes of tamarind and jaggery), delivered a beautiful harmony of sweet, sour, and mildly spicy flavors. The mango pieces were juicy and tender, while the gravy had that signature creamy texture and depth you expect from authentic Kerala sadhya dishes. The neer dosa — thin, lacy, and soft like a delicate crepe — proved to be the perfect companion. It soaked up the pullissery beautifully without overpowering it, letting every bite shine. The combination was so satisfying and well-balanced that by the end of it, our usual post-meal filter coffee felt completely unnecessary. The flavors lingered pleasantly, leaving us content and surprisingly full without any heaviness.The Mango Mania offerings at Banana Leaf strike a nice balance between familiar favorites (like aam ras) and more adventurous regional specials (like the pullissery). The portions were generous, the ingredients tasted fresh, and the execution stayed true to South Indian roots while highlighting the season’s best produce.If you’re a mango lover and enjoy authentic Kerala and South Indian vegetarian fare, this special menu is worth a visit while it lasts. Just come prepared — one taste of that Mango Pullissery with neer dosa, and you might skip the coffee too.
Rating: 4.5/5
Must-try: Mango Pullissery with Neer Dosa

featured_reviews.name: sagar jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was my third visit to Santosham, and it continues to be a great spot for comforting, authentic South Indian food!
If you are looking for a complete traditional experience, their unlimited South Indian Thali is a must-try at least once. It’s a beautifully simple, home-style meal that tastes amazing. The thali comes fully loaded with a variety of authentic items—hot puris, steamed rice, flavorful and piping hot Sambar, a wonderfully tangy Rasam, and traditional sabjis like a dry Beans and Carrot Poriyal and a comforting Cabbage Kootu. They round it out with crisp appalams, fresh curd, pickle, and a sweet Payasam to finish it off. Just a quick heads-up: they have different pricing for the unlimited thali on weekdays versus weekends.
While the thali is fantastic and incredibly generous, it is quite a heavy meal. Personally, since we lean more toward classic South Indian snacks rather than massive authentic meals, the thali is a 'try it once for the experience' item for us.
If you aren't super hungry or just prefer lighter fare, absolutely go for their Idli and Dosa options instead. They are perfectly prepared and hit the spot every time. I also have to give a massive shoutout to their Dal Wada—it is incredibly crispy on the outside, perfectly spiced, and just flat-out delicious.

Staff is very helpful, one of the staff saw I m not adding Green chutney on rice, he came and suggested to use green chutney over the rice and it really tasted so good 😊
Overall verdict: Come hungry for the grand unlimited thali at least once, but you'll find yourself coming back regularly for the stellar dosas, idlis, and that amazing dal wada!

featured_reviews.review_text:
The banana leaf thali is not just a meal – it’s an experience that blends flavor, tradition, and hospitality in the most wholesome way. Served on a fresh banana leaf, the thali immediately brings a sense of authenticity and connection to Indian culinary roots.

What makes it truly special is the variety. From fragrant rice and comforting dals to vibrant curries, tangy pickles, crispy papad, and a sweet finish, every dish complements the other beautifully. The balance of flavors – spicy, tangy, salty, and sweet – ensures that every bite feels satisfying. The banana leaf itself adds a subtle earthy aroma while also being eco-friendly and hygienic.

Another highlight is the cultural warmth associated with it. The way servers lovingly add refills, encouraging you to eat to your heart’s content, makes the experience feel both generous and personal.

Overall, the banana leaf thali is not just good – it’s nourishing, soulful, and a celebration of food as tradition. Whether you’re a food enthusiast or someone who loves comfort meals, it’s definitely worth trying.

I had a very disappointing experience at Udupi Restaurant, Ghatkopar East today.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Finally checked out the new The Rameshwaram Cafe and honestly… it felt like I was transported straight back to Hyderabad. If you’ve ever been to Rameshwaram there, you’ll know exactly what I mean..it's the same buzz, the same chaos, the same aroma of ghee hitting you the second you walk in. And I’m so glad to say, they’ve managed to recreate that exact feeling here in Mumbai.
See Location-wise, it couldn’t get better. It’s literally right at Churchgate, inside the iconic Eros building, barely a minute’s walk from the station...its super convenient whether you’re coming after work or just craving a quick South Indian fix.
The food is CRAZY GOOD! Simple South Indian dishes but elevated with insane amounts of ghee and flavour.
Some absolute must-tries:
Ghee Podi Idli, Benne Masala Dosa,Vada sambhar,Thatte Idli &  Filter Coffee (and even the softy version!) (surprisingly a highlight)
Yes, there’s a wait. Yes, it’s crowded.
Yes, it’s a little chaotic. But that’s exactly what makes it Rameshwaram! :)

featured_reviews.name: shaikh almas
featured_reviews.review_text:
Rameshwaram Cafe is an absolute delight for South Indian food lovers! I tried the dosa, idli, medu vada, and sheera—and every single item was outstanding.
The dosa was perfectly crisp with generous ghee, the idlis were super soft and fluffy, and the medu vada was crunchy on the outside and soft inside, served piping hot. The sheera was rich, flavorful, and tasted freshly made—just the right balance of sweetness and ghee.
And special mention to the tea—hands down one of the best teas I’ve had. Perfectly brewed and incredibly refreshing.
Cleanliness, quality, and consistency really stand out here. Even with the crowd, the service was quick and efficient. Totally worth the hype and a must-visit place for authentic South Indian food. Will definitely come back again! ☕🥞✨

- filter coffee very good
Service:
- Inspite of empty tables in AC, I was made to sit in the gallery just because I was alone
- They do not serve regular water at all even on request, you’re forced to buy PLASTIC bottled water… like why?
- Service staff was humble and well trained but felt like they are trained to ensure good ratings, which is fine, but the food and overall eating experience should genuinely match that

Atmosphere:
-Everything felt very commercial

The idli was super soft and fluffy, just like it should be. It melted in the mouth and tasted even better with the sambar. The chutneys were fresh and added great taste to the meal.
